_README: Pulse-streamer build manifest -- the SINGLE source describing the requested geometry.
This period-table engine requires a new build and board qualification. The host validates it and
the server also verifies the matching LAYOUT_FINGERPRINT from hardware.  It is not a
runtime tuning surface.  Only a separately approved, evidence-driven RTL recovery may
change these values, regenerate zlc_geometry.vh/geom.tcl, rebuild, and requalify hardware.
estimate_resources.bat may inspect a proposed recovery geometry; it grants no authority
to replace the programmed bitstream or claim that routing and timing passed.
Every 'params' field is folded into the geometry FINGERPRINT (CTRL word 63) except the
host-only cap ttl_delay_max_ticks, so a host packing for one geometry REFUSES a bitstream
built for another.  Editing this file alone only makes startup fail; it never changes the
running FPGA.  The explicit board.lanes indices generate the host target and validate
both the RTL top mapping and XDC; declaration order in either projection has no meaning.
See '_field_docs' below for what each field means.  '_README' and '_field_docs' are

_field_docs.uart_baud: USB_UART baud shared by host and generated RTL. The onboard CH340C is specified for 460800 bps continuous transfer; changing this requires rebuilding/programming the FPGA and restarting its server, not a host-only setting.
_field_docs.fpga_part: Xilinx part string (e.g. xc7a35tfgg484-2).  Selects the resource budgets (LUT/FF/DSP/RAMB36) the estimator checks against and the synthesis target.
_field_docs.clock_hz: FPGA fabric clock in Hz.  50 MHz -> 20 ns per tick.  THE single source for the compile + runtime tick rate (all timing is in ticks); must equal the board oscillator + the XDC create_clock.
_field_docs.target_pct: Resource-budget target for estimate_resources (percent of each resource the geometry may use).  The capacity report flags any axis over this.
_field_docs.channel_count: Physical lane count from board.lanes: leading TTL outputs, DAC data bits and latch clocks. Row masks and TTL delays use only channel_count - bus_count*(bus_width+1); clocks use bus-index enable bits. Changing pins requires matching manifest/XDC/top and a new build, not this number alone.
_field_docs.num_slots: Number of SCAN slots (s0..s{n-1}) one scan point carries: a duration slot holds a row's tick count, a DAC slot an offset-binary code, and a row or bus action names the slot that supplies its value.  Power of two (the scan BRAM reads one whole slot vector per access).
_field_docs.tick_width: Bit width of a row duration and of a scan slot value (the 20 ns-resolution tick count).  Fixed at 32 (the row field, the scan slots and the CTRL words are 32-bit); 32 bits ~= 85 s per row at 50 MHz.
_field_docs.max_rows: Maximum number of period rows in one program (one row per authored period; a bracket body is stored once).  Power of two; sizes the row BRAM (row_words x 32 bits wide, max_rows deep).  512 -> ROW_ADDR_WIDTH = 9.
_field_docs.bank_size: Scan points per ping-pong bank. TWO banks form the resident streaming window: the host freezes the complete logical table before FIRE, preloads the first two chunks, then refills each released bank while the FPGA remains the point-timing owner. This is a physical bank/chunk and refill-slack bound, not a logical scan-length limit. Power of two; sizes the scan BRAM (2*bank_size deep).
_field_docs.bus_count: Number of analog DAC buses (each = bus_width parallel output bits + one da_clk latch strobe).  4 buses (dipole / bias_x / bias_y / bias_z on this board).
_field_docs.bus_width: Bits per DAC bus.  10 -> 1024 codes in OFFSET-BINARY: code 0 = negative full scale, 512 = 0 V (idle/safe), 1023 = +full scale.
_field_docs.max_loops: Loop-table entries per program = how many brackets one Pulse may hold (nested or disjoint).  Each entry is a register triple (first row, last row, count) the row walker follows.
_field_docs.loop_depth: How many brackets may be nested inside one another; the row walker keeps one remaining-count register per level.  Must not exceed max_loops.
_field_docs.evt_fifo_depth: Per-TTL-CHANNEL event-FIFO depth = max output TOGGLES in flight per channel while a delay is applied (out[t] = in[t-d]).  Power of two (ring pointer).  Deeper = denser delayable pulse trains, more distributed RAM (LUTRAM).  NOT the delay LENGTH (that is ttl_delay_max_ticks).
_field_docs.bus_evt_fifo_depth: Per-DAC-BUS action-FIFO depth = max RESOLVED bus actions (edge/ramp) in flight while a bus delay is applied (density-independent: one dense ramp = 1 action).  Power of two.
_field_docs.delay_region_words: Reserved 32-bit words in the R_DELAY register region (one delay word per delay-eligible signal: channels then buses).  Must be >= the TTL pin count (channel_count less each bus's data and latch pins) + bus_count, as wire.check_rtl_assumptions checks; 128 gives headroom and a stable layout across configs.
_field_docs.ttl_delay_max_ticks: HOST-side validation cap on a single output delay, in ticks (the 32-bit R_DELAY field; (1<<31)-1 ~= 42.9 s at 20 ns).  Host-only -- it is NOT folded into the fingerprint, so tuning it needs no rebuild.  The real working limit is toggles IN FLIGHT (the FIFO depths above), checked at fire time.
